requirement: Records communal purchases, calculates each roommate's portion, and links to external payment services (Venmo, Zelle, Apple Cash) for repayment. Always shows the list of past purchases and a confirmation when a roommate pays back.

Always shows a wishlist of future shared purchases. "Add item" opens a pop-up for price, optional link, and optional description of why it's needed. Clicking an item shows details; only its creator can edit or delete it.

List of chores that starts empty. "Add task" takes a name, description, and either a date and time (one-time) or a day of the week and time (recurring), with a calendar picker. Creator picks the responsible roommate, or the system rotates the chore through roommates in turn. Sort and filter by date added, alphabetical, or assignee.

Each chore shows whether it is done and the date it was marked complete. Chores can be marked done when completed or once the date passes. Upcoming chores appear on each user's home page and link to the chore's details.

On a chore assigned to them, a user can pick another roommate, choose one of that roommate's chores, write a reason, and submit a swap request (or request a skip). The recipient sees the proposal and message, accepts or declines, and can reply; the response notifies the requester.

Always visible, with a list view and a calendar view. "Add event" takes a name, date, reminder, tagged roommates, location, and color. Clicking an event shows all details; only the creator can edit. Events can be sorted by color. Chores appear on the calendar showing the task name and who is assigned that occurrence.

Sticky-note board next to the calendar, used to share plans and check with roommates before hosting guests. Clicking the board enlarges it. A note can tag a calendar event and links to it. Roommates can reply to notes, and the board and calendar update in real time.

Notifications from other roommates' actions land in one of five sections: (1) chore swap requests and chore updates, (2) money requests and payments, (3) new items added to the expense tracker, (4) system updates, (5) calendar updates and new board comments. Every notification has a "Check it out" button that opens the related part of the app. Swap requests show a red alert in the top bar.

One-glance snapshot of this week's calendar, the latest notifications, and recent board comments; clicking any of them opens the full feature. An AI reads the snapshot at sign-in and gives a 1-2 sentence update or recommended action.
A top bar is always shown with Home, Settings, and links to each section, leaving out the page the user is currently on.
Each profile shows a photo, contact information and social media, allergies, preferred payment platform, and other important information.
Roommates can see each other's work and school schedules on the shared calendar, along with upcoming plans that affect the apartment.
Users can create custom tasks beyond the preset chore and finance types.
Users can send reminders about tasks that haven't been done.
Roommates post food and cleaning supplies that need restocking, and the system shows whose turn it is to buy.
Roommates can receive the app's notifications about chores, payments, and other updates on their phones.
Tasks can be sorted to show what hasn't been done in a while.
Import calendars from and export calendars to other services.
The site offers both a light mode and a dark mode.
Colors can be customized per account.
Sync shared calendars with outside calendars and pay roommates back directly inside the app.
Connect to messaging platforms so messages can be sent over data.

A version for whole apartment complexes: complex-wide announcements dashboard and shared calendar, Reels (approved short-form videos of complex events to attract tenants), easy lease renewal, and easy help requests.
No shared texting thread; the app is not meant to be a texting or communication platform.
No roommate location sharing or tracking (Life360-style).
No sub-groups within a household, since they would encourage cliques between roommates.
No chat between different roommate groups.
